x: Heatley came up from ninth to take over the lead and to lower the course record by 17 seconds, whilst Pat, despite an excellent run, was pushed back to eighth by other "big-guns", namely Connolly, Craig, Langridge, and Herring.

It was quite a tonic to see him loping along uphill and down dale to record 28:35 which was a new Club record and a time beaten only by Internationals of such class as Kilby(Coventry) Bullivant (Derby) Craig (Blackpool) Freary (Bolton) and Tulloh (Portsmouth).

Bill's best London to Brighton run was in the National event of April 1962 when he recorded 6th fastest time on the long stage 9 with only Kilby, Bullivant, Craig, Freary and Tulloh (all internationals) being faster.
